title: Border Patrol agents kill VA nurse Alex Pretti during Minneapolis protest
synopsis: On Jan. 24, 2026, VA intensive-care nurse Alex Pretti was shot and killed by federal border agents during Minneapolis protests tied to Operation Metro Surge. DHS later told Congress that two federal officers fired their weapons, and reporting said Pretti had been filming and helping a pepper-sprayed woman when agents moved in. The killing became a flashpoint for protests demanding an end to the ICE surge.

title: Operation Metro Surge: Minneapolis and St. Paul sue to stop ICE crackdown
synopsis: In January 2026, Minneapolis and St. Paul sued the federal government to halt Operation Metro Surge, alleging unconstitutional immigration raids and excessive force by DHS agents. The lawsuit described widespread raids, arrests of bystanders, and enforcement actions at sensitive locations, while residents and officials reported mass protests and disruption across the Twin Cities. Continued raids and use-of-force incidents kept the operation under national scrutiny.

title: Amazon pays $40M for 'Melania' documentary, sparking ethics concerns
synopsis: Amazon MGM bought the documentary 'Melania' for a reported $40 million and committed roughly $35 million in marketing ahead of its Jan. 30, 2026 theatrical release. Amazon's own materials note the film is directed by Brett Ratner and made with Melania Trump's participation. Commentators criticized the scale and timing of the deal as a potential influence-buying conflict of interest.

title: TPS for Somalis ended as Trump targets Ilhan Omar amid Minneapolis crackdown
synopsis: During the Minneapolis crackdown, Trump repeatedly attacked Somalis and Rep. Ilhan Omar; a December 2025 cabinet-meeting account described him calling Somali immigrants 'garbage' and attacking Omar. On Jan. 14, 2026, DHS issued a Federal Register notice terminating Somalia's Temporary Protected Status effective March 17, 2026. On Jan. 27, Omar was sprayed with an unknown substance at a Minneapolis town hall amid protests over ICE raids.

title: DOJ misses Epstein files deadline under Transparency Act
synopsis: The Epstein Files Transparency Act required DOJ to release all unclassified Epstein-related records by Dec. 19, 2025, but by early January DOJ said it was still reviewing more than two million documents and had released only a fraction. Lawmakers and advocates criticized the delay, and the House Oversight Committee voted to hold Bill and Hillary Clinton in contempt for refusing to testify in late January. In court, Ghislaine Maxwell filed a sealed motion to vacate her conviction, prompting orders to redact filings before they are made public.

title: Trump orders drone strike that kills Iranian General Qasem Soleimani
synopsis: On January 3, 2020, the United States killed Iranian General Qasem Soleimani in a drone strike near Baghdad airport on orders from President Trump. The strike escalated tensions with Iran, sparked fears of wider conflict, and raised questions about legal authority and congressional oversight. The killing was widely described as a major escalation in U.S.–Iran confrontation.

title: Reports of Russian bounties on U.S. troops trigger denial and backlash
synopsis: In late June 2020, news outlets reported that U.S. intelligence assessed Russia offered bounties to Taliban-linked militants to kill U.S. and allied troops in Afghanistan. The Trump White House said the president was not briefed and questioned the intelligence, sparking bipartisan outrage and scrutiny over whether the administration responded to the reports. The controversy highlighted intelligence disputes and concerns about national security decision‑making.

title: Trump Tower Moscow Deal Cover-Up Revealed in Cohen Guilty Plea
synopsis: Michael Cohen pleaded guilty to lying to Congress about the Trump Organization's pursuit of a Trump Tower Moscow project, admitting negotiations continued well into the 2016 campaign despite public denials of Russia ties. The project involved outreach to Kremlin-linked officials, creating a conflict between private business interests and campaign messaging. The plea placed the cover-up at the center of the Russia investigation and raised questions about foreign influence.

title: Michael Cohen Testifies Trump Is a 'Con Man' and Details Hush Money
synopsis: In public testimony to the House Oversight Committee, former Trump lawyer Michael Cohen called Trump a 'con man,' 'cheat,' and 'racist' and described directing hush money payments and efforts to conceal the Trump Tower Moscow negotiations. Cohen presented documents and said he had lied to Congress at Trump's direction. The hearing painted a picture of a president using personal lawyers for political cover and financial manipulation.

title: Trump Commutes Roger Stone Sentence After Conviction for Lying to Congress
synopsis: Trump commuted longtime ally Roger Stone's prison sentence after Stone was convicted of lying to Congress and witness tampering in the Russia investigation. The move spared Stone from prison just days before he was due to report. Critics argued it rewarded loyalty and undercut the justice system.

title: Supreme Court Lets Prosecutors Seek Trump Tax Returns After Years of Stonewalling
synopsis: After years of fighting subpoenas, the Supreme Court ruled that prosecutors could seek Trump's financial records, including tax returns, and that Congress could pursue them under limits. Trump had broken with modern precedent by refusing to release his returns and arguing broad immunity. The rulings were a legal setback to his secrecy strategy.

title: SharpieGate: Trump Displays Altered Hurricane Dorian Map to Claim Alabama Threat
synopsis: After falsely warning that Alabama was in Hurricane Dorian's path, Trump displayed a hurricane forecast map altered with a Sharpie to show Alabama in the cone. The doctored image contradicted official forecasts and drew criticism from scientists and NOAA officials. The incident became a symbol of misinformation during a public safety threat.

title: Report: Trump Suggested 'Nuking Hurricanes' to Stop Them Hitting the U.S.
synopsis: A report said Trump suggested using nuclear weapons to disrupt hurricanes before they hit the United States. The idea was widely dismissed as dangerous and unworkable, and Trump later denied the report. The episode underscored a pattern of impulsive, pseudo-scientific proposals in crisis discussions.

title: Trump Claims Finland 'Rakes' Forests to Prevent Wildfires
synopsis: While discussing California wildfires, Trump claimed Finland prevents fires by 'raking' forest floors. Finnish officials said no such advice was given, and experts noted the claim was misleading. The remark fueled ridicule and confusion about wildfire science.

title: Trump Claims Wind Turbine Noise Causes Cancer
synopsis: At a GOP dinner, Trump said the noise from wind turbines causes cancer and claimed turbines tank property values. The assertion has no scientific basis, but it spread widely as another example of energy misinformation. The comments were mocked and corrected by experts.

title: 'Tim Apple' Gaffe: Trump Misnames Tim Cook in White House Meeting
synopsis: During a White House meeting on technology and jobs, Trump referred to Apple CEO Tim Cook as 'Tim Apple' while praising investment in U.S. manufacturing. The slip went viral and became shorthand for his public misstatements. It was framed as a gaffe rather than policy.

title: 'Hamberders' Tweet After Fast-Food White House Feast
synopsis: After hosting the Clemson Tigers with a fast-food spread during the shutdown, Trump tweeted that he served over 1,000 'hamberders' before correcting the spelling. The tweet went viral and became another emblem of his social-media sloppiness. The episode reinforced perceptions of spectacle over substance.
